Use feature overlap to build a simple peer-implied move
joined = premarket.merge(features, on='ticker') pairs = joined.merge(joined, how='cross', suffixes=('_target', '_peer')) pairs = pairs[pairs['ticker_target'] != pairs['ticker_peer']].copy() pairs['similarity'] = ( (pairs['sector_target'] == pairs['sector_peer']).astype(int) * 2 + (pairs['theme_target'] == pairs['theme_peer']).astype(int) * 3 + (pairs['market_bucket_target'] == pairs['market_bucket_peer']).astype(int) ) pairs = pairs[pairs['similarity'] > 0].sort_values(['ticker_target', 'similarity'], ascending=[True, False]) pairs['weighted_move'] = pairs['premarket_move_peer'] * pairs['similarity'] expected = pairs.groupby('ticker_target', as_index=False).agg( similarity_sum=('similarity', 'sum'), weighted_sum=('weighted_move', 'sum'), closest_peers=('ticker_peer', lambda x: ', '.join(x.head(3))), ) expected['peer_implied_move'] = expected['weighted_sum'] / expected['similarity_sum'] readthrough = expected.merge(joined[['ticker', 'premarket_move']], left_on='ticker_target', right_on='ticker') readthrough['actual_minus_peer_implied'] = readthrough['premarket_move'] - readthrough['peer_implied_move'] show_df(readthrough[['ticker_target', 'premarket_move', 'peer_implied_move', 'actual_minus_peer_implied', 'closest_peers']].round(2))
